text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - UK shares finished slightly lower on Thursday as some investors decided to lock in profits ahead of next Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve monetary meeting -- deliberations which could prompt a near-term rise in U.S. interest rates.
The FTSE 100 index closed 5.7 points lower at 4,681.2.

FRANKFURT - German shares were saddled with losses in bourse trade on Thursday, ending the session down in listless trading as the market searched for fuel to launch a new advance on record levels. The 30-share DAX index ended the bourse session down 11.58 points at 3,562.11 points. In post-bourse trade the index fell 23.72 to 3,564.85.

PARIS - French shares edged up to a fresh closing record on Thursday, helped by a positive reaction in the U.S. financial markets to inflation and other economic data. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 1.38 points at 2,776.01, surpassing Wednesday's closing record of 2,774.63 after erasing its early losses. ZURICH - Swiss shares recovered after a weaker start to post a fourth-straight record close. "Sell in May and go away does not seem to apply here," a dealer said, adding Swiss shares moved up after an early correction as U.S. bonds rose on latest U.S. data. "Wall Street seems to be in for another rise, so the prospects are good" for Switzerland, the dealer said. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 6.24 points to 3,245.92.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed moderately lower on Thursday as the yen's rapid advance against the dollar clouded prospects for export-driven issues, brokers said. The weak sentiment was further hurt by the news that Tokyo prosecutors had raided Nomura Securities Co Ltd's headquarters as part of an investigation into suspected illegal payoffs, raising concerns about other brokerages, they said. The 225-share Nikkei average gave up 153.41 points to close at 20,056.31.

HONG KONG - A flurry of profit-taking in afternoon trade pushed Hong Kong stocks to a sharply lower close on Thursday, with a drop in HSBC Holdings Plc shares forcing the Hang Seng Index to give up some of its record ground. The blue chip index ended 111.68 points lower to 14,041.90 after rising to an early record high of 14,167.01.
SYDNEY - A patchy Australian share market closed slightly lower on Thursday, weighed down by a volatile bank sector.
The All Ordinaries index lost 5.4 points to 2,525.0.

Bank sector leader National Australia Bank posted a 14.1 percent jump in first half net profit to A$1.14 billion (US$889 million) but warned that margins were down across the board, confirming a similarly downbeat forecast made on Wednesday by rival big four bank, Westpac Banking Corp, when it reported.
JOHANNESBURG - South African shares finished well down after directionless trade on Thursday as profit-taking and some negativity from disappointing results knocks prices.
Golds slipped on the back of a dull bullion price, failing to hold small gains made earlier this week.

Dealers said sentiment negative, but local bond market and rand seen providing some positive cue on Friday. Industrials closed down 53.3 points at 8,440.6, golds were off 15.4 points at 1,254.7 and the all-share closed down 41.4 points at 7,173.1.
